purpose: This medication is used to treat diarrhea in adults. It helps slow down the movement in your intestines so your body can absorb more water and firm up your stools. It is usually used for short-term relief when diarrhea is uncomfortable or disruptive to your daily life.
how_it_works: Difenoxin works by slowing down the muscles in your intestines, which helps reduce how fast stool moves through your gut. Atropine is added in a small amount to discourage people from misusing or abusing the medication, since difenoxin is related to opioid drugs. Together, they help calm your digestive system and reduce diarrhea symptoms.
common_side_effects: Common side effects can include nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, headache, and stomach discomfort. Some people may also feel lightheaded or have trouble sleeping. These effects are usually mild and tend to go away as your body adjusts.
warnings: This medication can be habit-forming, so it should only be used exactly as prescribed and not for longer than recommended. Do not take more than the prescribed dose. Avoid alcohol and other sedatives while taking this medication. Do not use it if you have severe liver disease, certain bowel infections, or in children under 12. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Seek emergency help if you notice signs of overdose such as extreme drowsiness, slow breathing, or confusion.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 2 tablets taken right away, followed by 1 tablet after each loose stool, but no more than 8 tablets in a single day. Treatment is typically limited to just a few days. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing can vary based on your situation.
